summary: Equities: US large cap median 6.3% (n=7) trails global equity at 6.8% (n=5) and EM equity at 8.1% (n=6); US small cap sits at 6.0% (n=6). Private equity has the highest median, 9.7% (n=5).

Bonds: cash 3.6% (n=6), intermediate Treasuries 4.8% (n=7), IG corporate 5.2% (n=5), high yield 5.5% (n=7), EM USD sovereign 5.7% (n=8); credit adds little over Treasuries, matching tight-spread commentary.

Widest disagreements, ranked by IQR (rows with n≥4): commodities 225bp, US small cap 188bp, private equity 155bp, private credit 143bp, EM equity 122bp; tightest are US TIPS 37bp and EM local debt 41bp.

Stated stances lean underweight US large cap (six to one) and overweight EM (seven to one) and Japan equity (five to one); PIMCO's underweights in high yield, loans and private credit oppose GSAM's overweights.

This site's LTCMA sits furthest from a well-populated median on commodities: 3.5% vs 5.2% (170bp below, n=7). UK equity (7.0% vs 9.0%, two publishers) and gold (3.3% vs 1.6%, one publisher) are thin comparisons.
This site's LTCMA is above the public median on US TIPS (4.5% vs 3.8%, n=4), below on US high yield (5.0% vs 5.5%, n=7) and US large cap (6.0% vs 6.3%, n=7).
Next FOMC: a hold priced at 83.5% on both venues, a 25bp hike at 15.5-16.0%; zero 2026 cuts near-certain (95.8-95.9%), at odds with GSAM, UBS and BNY easing calls; Vanguard's higher-for-longer fits.

US recession in 2026 is priced at 3.5% (Kalshi) and 6.5% (Polymarket), consistent with GSAM's soft landing; Polymarket gives Democrats the House at 92.5% and Senate at 64.5%, relevant to fiscal-support calls.

A19.why: Favor long euro versus USD; EURUSD forecast rising to 1.20 by mid-2026.

A23.why: Euro favoured on narrowing rate differentials and improved European fiscal momentum.

A19.why: Preference for high-yielding currencies as risk appetite broadens in FX markets; not specifically framed as EM.

A23.why: Oil expected to trade within a moderate range.

divergence_rule: public IQR >= 150bp with n >= 4, or >= 1 overweight and >= 1 underweight stance

divergences.label: US large cap
divergences.headline: US large cap: stances lean underweight six to one; public numbers split 4.9-5.5% versus 6.4-7.6% around a 6.3% median.

bull.argument: BNY's Grinold-Kroner build, the range high at 7.6%, pairs buyback-heavy income with AI-boosted earnings growth at constant valuations. Fidelity's 6.4% weighs AI-boosted GDP growth against elevated margins and reverting valuations. BII's high-conviction overweight cites AI-driven earnings and supportive macro. T. Rowe Price's 6.4% (five-year) sits just above the median despite an underweight stance.
bull.data_used: Net payout yield (dividends plus buybacks), AI-driven earnings and GDP growth, constant or only partly reverting valuation multiples.

bear.argument: Invesco's 4.9%, the range low, nets a large valuation mean-reversion drag against strong earnings and buybacks; Vanguard's 5.1% reflects valuations rising from already elevated levels; State Street's 5.5% tempers its building blocks for valuation. PIMCO sees a near-zero equity risk premium, with high-quality bonds offering a comparable Sharpe ratio; Lazard expects allocators to rotate away from US equities.
bear.data_used: Starting valuations with mean reversion, equity risk premium versus high-quality bond yields, dividend yield plus real earnings growth plus inflation.

divergences.what_to_watch: Whether forward multiples compress while AI-led earnings growth holds, and the earnings-yield gap over Treasuries; the split is mostly a valuation-path assumption.

divergences.label: US small cap
divergences.headline: US small cap: IQR of 188bp, second only to commodities; numbers 4.5-7.5% split on earnings growth and size premium.

bull.argument: GSAM is overweight on attractive valuations, anticipated rate cuts, accelerating earnings and a dealmaking revival. AQR's 7.4% and T. Rowe Price's 6.3% (five-year, a selective upgrade) also sit above the median. BNY has the range high, 7.5%, yet is underweight, citing a muted size premium as early-stage growth shifts to private markets.
bull.data_used: Relative valuation versus large caps, expected rate cuts, earnings acceleration and M&A (GSAM); real return plus inflation (AQR); factor-model size premium (BNY).

bear.argument: Invesco (underweight, 4.5%, the range low) sees less valuation drag than large caps but weak long-run earnings growth. Vanguard's 5.7% reflects a second-quarter rally that raised valuations, cutting its forecast much as for large caps. State Street's 5.1% sits below its own large-cap 5.5%, with higher volatility. All three are below the 6.0% median.
bear.data_used: Post-rally starting valuations, long-run earnings growth of smaller firms, higher expected volatility.

divergences.what_to_watch: Small-cap earnings growth versus large caps, relative valuation after the rally, and policy rates: zero 2026 Fed cuts are priced at 95.8-95.9% across Kalshi and Polymarket.

divergences.label: China equity
divergences.headline: China equity: only two public numbers, 5.8% and 8.7%; overweights cite valuations, Lazard sees fragility needing intervention.

bull.argument: GSAM is overweight on attractive valuations and light positioning, while warning that durability depends on earnings and flagging tariff and policy shocks. Amundi is overweight because lagging performance left valuations attractive. T. Rowe Price's 8.7% (five-year) pairs a high return with its highest equity volatility, helped by an EM earnings rebound.
bull.data_used: Starting valuations and investor positioning (GSAM, Amundi); EM earnings rebound and a high volatility assumption (T. Rowe Price, five-year horizon).

bear.argument: Lazard is underweight, arguing that China's apparent stability masks deeper weaknesses requiring meaningful government intervention. Invesco's 5.8% leans on its strongest currency tailwind to offset weak earnings growth and a negative buyback yield.
bear.data_used: Earnings growth, buyback yield (negative) and currency assumptions (Invesco); structural and policy assessment (Lazard).

divergences.what_to_watch: Chinese earnings revisions, net share issuance, the yuan against the dollar and the scale of policy support.

divergences.label: Japan equity
divergences.headline: Japan equity: five overweights, mostly on governance reform, versus one underweight; public numbers 6.3-8.6%, median 6.4% (n=3).

bull.argument: Invesco (overweight, 8.6%, the range high) cites improved valuations, stable earnings growth and a positive currency adjustment. Lazard and Mercer point to governance reform delivering results and improving profitability; GSAM adds Takaichi fiscal support, wage-led spending, buybacks and a retail shift into risk assets. Schroders is also overweight.
bull.data_used: Governance and profitability trends, buybacks, starting valuations, yen appreciation via currency adjustment, fiscal and wage dynamics.

bear.argument: Amundi is underweight, arguing the strong rally has stretched valuations despite solid fundamentals. BNY's 6.3%, just under the 6.4% median (n=3), reflects a lower real growth outlook only partly offset by an assumed yen appreciation.
bear.data_used: Post-rally valuations (Amundi); real growth outlook and yen appreciation assumption (BNY).

divergences.what_to_watch: Japanese ROE and buyback follow-through versus post-rally multiples, and USD/JPY, since Invesco's and BNY's numbers both lean on yen appreciation.

divergences.label: EM equity
divergences.headline: EM equity: seven overweights against Vanguard's 3.0% outlier; other public numbers cluster at 7.1-8.8%.

bull.argument: Robeco's 8.8% (five-year) makes EM its top asset class on trade rewiring; T. Rowe Price's 8.7% follows improving earnings momentum; BNY's 8.1% (overweight) cites growth, AI and dollar weakness. GSAM and BII add strong earnings, cheaper valuations and a softer dollar. Schroders and Amundi are overweight on stance.
bull.data_used: EM earnings momentum and growth premium, P/E discount to the US, dollar path, AI-related exposure, trade realignment.

bear.argument: Vanguard (underweight) has the range low, 3.0%: the strong EM rally lifted valuations, making EM its weakest equity forecast with the highest volatility. Invesco's 7.1% (neutral) sees a smaller valuation drag and better currency contribution, still below developed ex-US; Fidelity's 8.0% sits just under the median despite citing faster growth and cheaper valuations.
bear.data_used: Post-rally starting valuations and volatility (Vanguard); valuation drag and currency contribution (Invesco); growth and valuation inputs (Fidelity).

divergences.what_to_watch: EM forward earnings revisions against the post-rally re-rating, and the dollar's direction; Vanguard's gap to peers is a starting-valuation dispute.

divergences.label: US IG corporate
divergences.headline: US IG: five neutrals on tight spreads; public numbers 4.1-5.5% hinge on spread-widening versus carry assumptions.

bull.argument: Invesco's 5.5%, the range high, rests on a higher total yield than Treasuries with limited credit losses; Fidelity's 5.4% combines rates income and spread carry, though it stays neutral given tight spreads. GSAM is overweight on mid-cycle fundamentals, value in segments such as banks and rate cuts lifting total returns. Schroders is also overweight.
bull.data_used: All-in yield over Treasuries, spread carry net of expected defaults and downgrades, mid-cycle credit fundamentals, expected rate cuts (GSAM).

bear.argument: Vanguard is underweight: rich valuations leave its credit index (IG corporate plus government-related) with no forecast premium over Treasuries, at 4.8%. T. Rowe Price's 4.1% (five-year), the range low, reflects tight starting spreads and expected modest widening. Both sit below the 5.2% median.
bear.data_used: Starting spreads near historical tights, expected spread widening, forecast premium of credit over the Treasury index.

divergences.what_to_watch: IG spreads relative to historical tights and issuance volume; widening would back the low-end forecasts, stable spreads the carry-based ones.

divergences.label: US high yield
divergences.headline: US high yield: three overweights versus three underweights; carry from high yields against PIMCO's credit-loss-cycle warning.

bull.argument: Invesco and BNY (both 6.1%, the range high) start from high all-in yields and still net out credit losses and expected spread widening; BNY is neutral on stance. Fidelity's 5.9% balances higher income against losses and tight spreads. GSAM is overweight on strong credit metrics, contained defaults, a better ratings mix and supportive M&A. Schroders is also overweight.
bull.data_used: All-in yield, expected default and recovery losses, assumed spread widening (Invesco, BNY), credit metrics and ratings mix (GSAM).

bear.argument: PIMCO is underweight with high conviction: a credit loss cycle is beginning and tight spreads reflect complacency, notably in lower-quality, levered credit. Amundi, underweight, notes spreads near historic tights. Vanguard (5.2%, underweight) sees only a modest premium over Treasuries for higher volatility; State Street's 4.6%, the range low, models spread term structure and defaults; AQR is at 5.0%.
bear.data_used: Spreads near historical tights, default-cycle onset (PIMCO), spread term structure and default probabilities (State Street), premium versus Treasuries per unit of volatility.

divergences.what_to_watch: Default and recovery rates among lower-rated, levered issuers and the direction of HY spreads; US recession in 2026 is priced at 3.5% (Kalshi) and 6.5% (Polymarket).

divergences.label: Commodities
divergences.headline: Commodities: widest IQR of any row (225bp), with estimates split into 2.3-3.8% and 5.7-6.7% clusters.

bull.argument: AQR (6.7%, the range high, overweight) adds a long-run diversified-futures excess return, measured over more than a century, to real cash. Robeco's 5.8% (five-year) rests on geopolitical supply disruptions and dollar dynamics. Vanguard's 5.7% on the Bloomberg Commodity Index comes without specific commentary, though it flags higher energy prices as an inflation risk.
bull.data_used: Long-history futures excess return plus real cash yield (AQR); geopolitical supply shocks and the dollar (Robeco); energy-led inflation risk (Vanguard).

bear.argument: BNY's 2.3%, the range low, is roughly unchanged from last year, with little stated rationale. State Street's 3.2% builds from US inflation and dollar forecasts, long-term roll return and collateral return. Invesco's 3.8% is its lowest expected return of any asset class, framed as a diversifying return driver after a slight quarter-on-quarter improvement.
bear.data_used: Building blocks: collateral (cash) return, long-term roll return, US inflation and dollar forecasts (State Street); limited published rationale from BNY and Invesco.

divergences.what_to_watch: Roll yield (futures curve shape), collateral cash rates and whether energy-driven inflation persists; this site's LTCMA (3.5%) sits with the lower cluster.

divergences.label: Bank loans
divergences.headline: Bank loans: two public numbers (6.0%, 6.9%); GSAM's rate-relief overweight against PIMCO's leveraged-loss underweight.

bull.argument: GSAM is overweight: lower policy rates would ease interest burdens for floating-rate leveraged-loan issuers and improve coverage. Invesco's 6.9%, the higher of the two public numbers, starts from a high floating-rate yield partly offset by expected credit losses.
bull.data_used: Floating-rate all-in yield, expected credit losses, assumed policy-rate cuts improving interest coverage (GSAM).

bear.argument: PIMCO is underweight, expecting significantly higher losses in leveraged lending where floating-rate structures meet high leverage. T. Rowe Price's 6.0% (five-year) is the lower public number, though T. Rowe Price still ranks loans highest among public US fixed income on floating-rate carry with little duration.
bear.data_used: Leverage and floating-rate debt-service burden, expected loss rates (PIMCO); carry versus duration exposure (T. Rowe Price).

divergences.what_to_watch: Leveraged-loan default and recovery rates and interest coverage; GSAM's relief case needs cuts, while zero 2026 Fed cuts are priced at 95.8% (Kalshi) and 95.9% (Polymarket).

divergences.label: Private equity
divergences.headline: Private equity: highest median at 9.7% (n=5), but estimates span 6.6-10.5% on leverage, fee and premium assumptions.

bull.argument: BNY's 10.5%, the range high, was raised sharply on the illiquidity premium and private capital's role funding AI and infrastructure. T. Rowe Price's 9.8% (five-year) rests on an illiquidity premium over public equity. Amundi is overweight on an illiquidity premium net of fees but flags slower distributions. BII's overweight covers venture capital only.
bull.data_used: Illiquidity premium over listed equity net of fees; private capital's role in AI and infrastructure financing (BNY).

bear.argument: AQR's 6.6%, the range low, comes from a levered dividend-discount model net of fees, even after lower debt costs and multiple expansion lifted its estimate. State Street's 8.2% leverage-adjusts historical PE performance against listed equities, net of fees. Both sit below the 9.7% median.
bear.data_used: Levered dividend-discount model with explicit fee drag (AQR); leverage-adjusted historical PE-versus-listed performance (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: Realized net-of-fee PE returns versus listed equity, distribution pace, exit multiples and leveraged-financing costs.

divergences.label: Private credit
divergences.headline: Private credit: four overweights versus PIMCO's high-conviction underweight; public numbers 5.0-9.2%, median 6.6% (n=4).

bull.argument: T. Rowe Price's 9.2% (five-year), the range high, cites an illiquidity premium and structural demand for private capital; Fidelity's 6.9% (neutral) relies on floating income. GSAM sees yields above public markets with lower historical defaults; BII prefers credit with clear cash flows and lender protections. Amundi sees an attractive risk-adjusted alternative to liquid credit.
bull.data_used: Illiquidity premium, floating-rate yields net of fees and losses, historical default experience, structural demand for private capital.

bear.argument: PIMCO is underweight with high conviction, citing emerging stress in private corporate credit and middle-market direct lending: maturity extensions, PIK use and financial engineering. AQR's 5.0%, the range low, models it as levered floating-rate high yield, cut by narrower spreads and lower cash rates; State Street's 6.4% covers senior direct lending net of fees.
bear.data_used: Credit-stress indicators (PIK usage, maturity extensions); levered high-yield proxy with current spreads and cash rates (AQR); senior direct-lending premium (State Street).

divergences.what_to_watch: PIK share, non-accruals and amend-and-extend activity in middle-market direct lending, plus realized defaults and recoveries versus public high yield.

regimes.cycle_phase: Resilient expansion with AI-related investment, energy-driven inflation risks, and a higher-for-longer Fed
regimes.summary: Q2 risk rally stretched equity valuations and lowered long-run return forecasts; yields stable, credit rich. Vanguard stresses valuations are poor short-term timing signals and takes no tactical stance.

regimes.cycle_phase: Late-stage equity rally (third straight up year) with compressed risk premia and positive real cash rates
regimes.summary: Equity premia remain compressed, especially in the US, while bonds and cash offer positive real yields; AQR expects lower future equity excess returns but says estimates are not for market timing.

regimes.cycle_phase: Resilient growth with moderating inflation; elevated yields and possible further tightening
regimes.summary: Volatile markets amid geopolitics and Fed uncertainty under Warsh; resilient US earnings, elevated bond yields aiding income and diversification, rally broadening to small caps.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle rejuvenated expansion; bull market only six years old, potentially as long as 2009-2019 expansion
regimes.summary: Base case 'Great Rewiring' (50%): AI-driven, investment-led expansion with higher inflation; next five years supportive for risk-taking, not as late-cycle as widely believed.

regimes.cycle_phase: Late cycle with credit loss cycle beginning; resilient but fragmenting global economy amid geopolitical rupture and AI capex boom
regimes.summary: Baseline resilient growth with fat tails both ways; downside growth risks; favor high quality fixed income over reaching for risk.

regimes.cycle_phase: Late-cycle US slowdown hidden by AI-driven gains; geopolitical shock from the Iran war; policy normalizing in Japan
regimes.summary: Structural shifts: a weaker dollar, non-US outperformance and steeper developed-market curves. US resilience is doubtful, China is fragile, Europe's recovery is delayed and Japan is normalizing.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle with Fed easing; soft landing base case
regimes.summary: Base case soft landing with Fed cutting ~75bps by end-2026; AI capex and fiscal support offset labor weakness; elevated valuations call for active, diversified positioning.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle expansion with easing policy rates; growth uneven early 2026 then improving
regimes.summary: UBS expects a supportive 2026 backdrop: improving confidence, fiscal stimulus, fading tariffs, Fed cuts and AI capex driving equity gains, with a weaker dollar.

regimes.cycle_phase: Structural paradigm shift from globalization to modern mercantilism, combined with an AI capex boom and resource grab
regimes.summary: Bridgewater sees a new regime shaped by national self-interest and AI investment. AI capex supports US growth, but inflation risks are structurally higher, and portfolios built for the old era are fragile.

regimes.cycle_phase: Mid-cycle / steady expansion with easing policy
regimes.summary: Steady 2026 global growth led by resilient US (fiscal stimulus, AI capex), inflation stabilising near targets, broadly accommodative policy; overall market positioning neutral.

regimes.cycle_phase: Growth re-accelerating with policy support; diverging monetary/fiscal paths and gradual DM rate easing
regimes.summary: Expects re-accelerating growth backed by fiscal and monetary policy, AI-driven productivity gains, a structurally weaker dollar, and rising sovereign debt pressure steepening yield curves.

regimes.cycle_phase: Post-shock normalization: activity has stabilized after higher rates, but inflation persists and the outlook is uncertain
regimes.summary: Markets have absorbed higher rates and entered a more balanced but uncertain phase. Returns are stable to modestly lower, the fixed income outlook is less forgiving, and volatility assumptions are slightly higher.

regimes.cycle_phase: Structural: fragmentation, high debt and AI revolution; elevated macro volatility and inflation
regimes.summary: AI lifts long-term GDP growth and equity returns, but fragmentation, debt and energy transitions keep inflation and macro volatility above pre-Covid levels.

regimes.cycle_phase: Expansion with renewed Fed tightening; AI-led growth amid structurally higher long-term yields
regimes.summary: Pro-risk: overweight U.S. and EM equities on AI-driven earnings; markets overprice further Fed hikes; structural forces keep long yields high, so avoid long bonds; dollar stable-to-weaker.
